haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 before any counter is read or changed, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Limits are per customer and all keys share one budget, so the total is the customer's plan limit: 100 per minute on Standard.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After in seconds. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. The count is not incremented for a rejected request, so the 429 uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is reserved before forwarding, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, forwards the request anyway (fail open), and sends no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard gets 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED (open, awaiting product decision).
haiku-low.q8: In a Redis counter key rl:<customerId>:<minute>, shared by all six gateways. Redis expires each key 60 seconds after it is written.
haiku-low.q9: At each minute boundary, since the window is fixed and a new counter key starts each minute. Old keys expire after 60 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one Lua script that Redis executes atomically, so no other command can run in the middle.
haiku-low.q11: The Lua script reads Redis TIME and returns seconds until the next minute boundary. The gateway rounds up, minimum 1.
haiku-low.q12: Retrying the store is NOT STATED. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers on that response.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized, and no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Only one shared budget: limits are per customer, so all keys share it. Standard plan: 100 requests per minute total (Enterprise limit not stated).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds). The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. The count is not incremented for a denied request, so the 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is reserved before forwarding, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, forwards the request to the backend, and returns the response without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: OPEN, awaiting product decision (not decided).
sonnet.q8: In Redis, a shared counter keyed rl:<customerId>:<minute>. The key expires 60 seconds after it is written, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: It resets at each fixed one-minute clock boundary: a new minute uses a new counter key (and the old key expires after 60 s).
sonnet.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script in Redis, with a single shared counter. It reads the count, increments only if below the limit, otherwise denies. No separate INCR then compare.
sonnet.q11: The Lua script reads Redis TIME and returns the seconds until the next minute boundary. The gateway sends that value rounded up, minimum 1. It does not use the key's expiry.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The client gets no rate-limit information: no X-RateLimit headers, just the backend response.
